items: dict keyed by ana_01, ana_02, ... — sequential IDs. Each item is one discrete finding.
label: short name (under 60 chars).
content: full prose paragraph describing the finding. Include actual numbers. Write complete, readable prose — the Editor reads this to understand each finding.
type: one of distribution, ranking, group-diff, correlation, anomaly, trend.

calculation._description: object with file, lines, and output. Every finding MUST have this.
calculation.file: path to the script in code/ (e.g., 'code/answer_distribution.py').
calculation.lines: [start_line, end_line] — the line range in that script that produces this finding (1-indexed, inclusive).
calculation.output: the verbatim terminal output that the claim is drawn from.

based_on: array of upstream det_xx IDs from detective.json that this finding references. Empty array [] if none.

notable_instance._description: optional. Add only when a finding has one standout data point that a concrete example would make felt, not just understood. Most findings don't need this.
notable_instance.name: the specific item (e.g., 'Ace of Spades', 'Blinding Lights').
notable_instance.value: the metric that makes it notable (e.g., '20.1%', 'F minor + 0.51 danceability').
notable_instance.instance_ref: reference to a detective inst_xx ID if one was collected for this item (or omit if none).
notable_instance.why: why this specific example is the best illustration of the finding.

caveats: array of data quality warnings. Each has an id (ana_caveat_01, ...) and content.
